## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the brows
er sign-in, for example because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh

token
to a named account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - |
- |\n| `GET .../accounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the
project |\n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`
201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the defaul
t (`isDefault: true`), or both |\n| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |\
n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/server
s/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/
json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"client

ult`,
`needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### A

ddressing an account

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that
account or answers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA n
ame no account has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409`

with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at
most 64 characters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up

. Names are
unique on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A n

ame is your own label, and
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
*
**Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, th
e account's owner\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL
saved in the project.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServer
Url`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token f
ield is at most 16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before ea
ch run, or when the issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n
expired account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** pe

r person and server: 60, refilling at 120 an
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An
API key acts as the person who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedi
cated member who\nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accou

nts are project accounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals fr
curl -fsS -X PATCH \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n
-H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{ \"isDefault\": true }'\n```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which
reads the token from a file, an environment varia
ble or stdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud

-server-accounts-commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same t
ime with different defaults. A suite that has saved\naccounts in its settings runs as those accounts and ignores the default, so\n

check the suite's settings before relying on the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its store
d token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand it also
ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make ano

ther
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed
90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, an
d keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a\n`Sunset` date and

a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes
into keeps whatever r
ule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourc

eUrl`
and `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.
\nThe error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the\n[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshoo

ting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).
